units.title: Forecast: calm, fog forming overnight
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound, issued 06:00 ST. Today: light and variable winds, sunny spells, sea slight, swell 0.8 m and easing. Max 7 C. Tonight: clear and cold, a frost inland, calm. Mist and fog patches forming on coasts and over the Sound after midnight, locally dense near the islands by dawn, with visibility below 200 m at times. Fog expected to lift slowly through the morning. Confidence in the timing of clearance is low.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. Sea trials of our relief vessel were completed satisfactorily yesterday. A provisional daylight sailing to Kittering Holm at first light tomorrow remains under review with the Coastguard. A final weather check will be made at 05:00. If fog prevents a safe approach, the sailing will be held or postponed. Timetabled services are not affected, though the 07:10 may be delayed by fog. The relief vessel will not carry passengers.

units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard Marrow Sound. The beacon on Kittering Holm remains active. A daylight transfer is provisionally planned for first light tomorrow, subject to visibility and conditions at the east dock; a decision will be made early tomorrow morning and published here. All other vessels should keep clear of the Holm's east approaches from 05:00. Please do not gather at Gilliver or Port Ammet slipways.

units.title: Fog update for first light
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound, issued 18:00 ST. Update for tomorrow's first light. Mist and fog are now expected to form over the Sound from about 02:00, thickest between Gilliver and the outer islands. Visibility may fall below 100 m in places at dawn. Some models clear it by 07:30; others hold it until mid-morning. A light southerly breeze could arrive earlier and help. A further update will be issued at 04:30.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines, 19:30. Our relief vessel has arrived at Port Ammet, crewed and fuelled. The provisional first-light sailing to Kittering Holm has not been cancelled and has not been confirmed. The decision will follow the 04:30 forecast and the 05:00 check. We know many people are waiting for news. We will post it here as soon as we have it, whichever way it goes.

units.title: Five days after the contract ended, a boat waits on the fog
units.author: courier
units.text: Five days after the Kittering Holm clearance contract ended, a relief vessel is crewed and fuelled at Port Ammet for a first-light sailing that may or may not go. The Met Office forecasts fog on the Sound tonight and cannot say when it will lift. The Coastguard says it will decide on the morning.

units.author: courier
units.text: Grieve Land Services has not added to its statement that the contract 'concluded in accordance with its terms'. Asked again whether staff remained on the island, a spokesperson said the company was 'cooperating fully with the relevant authorities' and would say nothing further. Ardent Vale Holdings has not responded to any request this week.

units.author: courier
units.text: In Gilliver, the village hall has stayed open late every night. A volunteer has kept a tally on the wall: tea, 1,140 cups; telephone calls, 212; people who came in just to sit, 'too many to count'. The front was lit again last night, two lamps in most windows, all facing the Holm.

units.title: Live: Holm sailing decision due at dawn
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 12:15 ST. Sound Lines says its relief vessel is now at Port Ammet. The Coastguard says the plan for a first-light sailing to Kittering Holm is unchanged, and so is the caveat: fog. We'll keep this page open through the evening and into the night.

units.title: City lamps for an island crew
units.author: weypost
units.text: Lamps have begun appearing in windows in Weyhaven too, following the Gilliver custom, as people wait for news of the crew on Kittering Holm. Residents of one tower block in the city have put tealights in jars on a stairwell landing. A caretaker said he would 'allow it for this week, fire regulations permitting'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 20:00 ST. The Met Office's evening update says fog will form after about 02:00 and may be thick near the islands at dawn. The Coastguard says a sailing can't be confirmed tonight. A spokesperson: 'We would rather tell families the truth at five in the morning than a hopeful guess at eight in the evening.'

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 22:30 ST. A listener on the Gilliver front describes the lights on the Holm as 'still there, three or four of them'. The Coastguard will not comment on what can or can't be seen from the shore. Our next update will follow the 04:30 forecast. If you're in Gilliver tonight, the hall is open.

units.title: Reminder: check your contact details
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Grieve Land Services payroll. This is a reminder to check that the contact details held for you are correct. Statements for closed contracts will be sent to the address on file. If you have moved, please update your details through the portal. This mailbox is not monitored. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Last chance: lantern event ends tonight!
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Hello again! Our long nights lantern event ends at midnight, so don't miss out. Our team's favourite pick this week: the two-mantle storm lantern, bright enough to see the whole camp by. Thank you to everyone who answered our survey. Your top tip for remote sites was 'keep a light on', which we couldn't have put better ourselves! The Camp Supply team

units.title: Tomorrow
units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: Hello. This will be the last time I write unless there is news. The relief boat is at Port Ammet and the decision on sailing will be made at five tomorrow morning, depending on the fog. I'll be at Gilliver, not to report on the boat but on the village, which has kept its lights on all week. I have written nothing about your crew that I couldn't stand up. I hope you're all able to read this. Nell Ashdown

units.title: tomorrow, maybe
units.author: sam
units.text: the radio says maybe tomorrow, first thing, if the fog lets them. I'm driving to Gilliver tonight with a flask. I know they've said not to come to the slipway and I won't, I'll stay up by the hall. Mum's made me take her old tartan blanket. the dog is coming because he refused not to. whatever happens tomorrow, I'm proud of you. love, S x

units.title: Fine
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Sorry. The reporter from the Courier said the boat might go at first light. A man from the shop in my friend's building has offered me a seat in his cousin's bread van at four, so I'm going to wait at the hall with everyone else. I've packed his good coat because he'll have ruined his. If he's with you tonight, please tell him I'm fine. That's all I've ever wanted to say. Ana

units.title: From the hall
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Chief. I'm in Gilliver Hall on a plastic chair, with about sixty people and the worst tea on the Sound. There's someone here with a dog and a tartan blanket who says they're your family, so I've introduced myself and we've shared a flask. Nobody's saying anything clever. Boat might go at five, depending on the fog. I'll be here either way.

units.title: Every window
units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: I might be wrong about a lot of things, I've said that. I'm not wrong about this. I walked the whole Gilliver front tonight on the way to work and the lights are on in every window. Every one, even the empty shop and the chapel. The fog came in over the water just after midnight and the lamps are smudges in it now. I hope it lifts. Morrow

units.title: From the archive: the missing reel, again
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note. Several readers have asked again about the microfilm reel missing for one winter in the 1890s. It is still missing. We have checked the bindery list, the 1968 transfer list and the basement. The paper copies for that winter were lent to the Lights Board survey in 1953 and returned 'incomplete', according to a note in the loans book. We do not know which pages. G. Faulds

units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: March 1895: a correction. Your correspondent wrote last month that the timber camp's men came over 'a fortnight early, in two boats'. He is told by a harbour family that it was one boat, and in January, not February, and that 'they had waited a long while for it'. He regrets the error, and has resolved to count nothing further without a witness.

units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk note. Someone has added to the article that the camp clerk's ledger 'ends mid-sentence'. It does not. It ends with a complete sentence and a transcriber's note, which I have checked against the Society's photocopy. Please do not improve primary sources. Whether the clerk came home is a separate question, and the records we hold do not answer it. Pell

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: Did the lamp ever bring anyone home? Mrs J. (b. 1899), second visit: 'Once.' [long pause] 'My uncle, in the fog year. He came up the shore road at four in the morning with no boat and no coat and walked straight to our window. He said he'd seen our lamp from the Holm.' [pause] 'You can't see the Holm from our house, mind. Never could.'

units.title: LBC-0977: Gilliver front, lamps (this week)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogue no. LBC-0977. Date: this week. Location: Gilliver front, facing the Holm. Kit: handheld recorder, two omnis. Recordist: dunlin_rec. Duration 22 min. Content: people talking quietly on the harbour wall, a dog, a kettle at the hall door, gulls, the evening ferry's horn. Recorded in daylight and at dusk only, at the recordist's request. Curator's note: no anomalies. Catalogued as 'community ambience'.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Jany. 9th. Frost. Roll at dusk, 6 men and myself and Coad. The boat has not come. Lamps lit at three. We have burnt the far stack for warmth and the yard is bright as a fair. Coad says the agent's boat will come on the first calm day and to have our things by the jetty. I have put the ledger in the oilcloth with the pay box.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Jany. 13th. Calm at last, and fog. Roll at dusk 6 men. A boat heard but not seen off the jetty about noon, oars, near. We lit every lamp we have and called till we were hoarse. It went away up the Sound. Coad says tomorrow. I have the ledger ready. [Transcriber's note: no further entries. The ledger was handed in at the Courier office in 1931 by a Gilliver family, who did not say how they came by it.]

units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Feb. 2. Fog all day thick as wool. No boats out. Jory and me sat with Mother. Toward night we heard a boat's engine out by the Holm side, slow, going round and round like a man looking for the harbour. Jory went down and lit the end lamp on the quay. Engine stopped. In the morning nobody in Gilliver was missing a boat, nor in Lisle.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Mar. 6. 00:00 wind NW 4, clear. 02:00 wind NW 4, lamp burning well. 03:15 lamp trimmed. Remarks: walkers on the shore road, one only, standing at the stile below the tower, at the beam's edge. Rowe away on leave. I did not hail. I lit the lamp in the kitchen window, as the Gilliver people do, and went back up. Logged here. E.S.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Swell at dawn 0.9 m, wind calm, pressure 1031. A perfect morning for anything except tomorrow morning, if you follow me. On my reckoning air temperature and dew point will be only two degrees apart by midnight, with the sea at 9 C. That's the recipe. I'll post at 04:30 tomorrow with whatever I can see from the point, if anything.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: I have been asked by several people whether I think 'the boat will go'. I am a retired teacher, not a forecaster. What I can say is that the Lisle school has put lamps in all eleven classroom windows facing the water, and the children made the shades. They are not very good shades. They are lit.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Not a forecaster either, but tide tables I can do. High water at the Holm tomorrow is a little after seven, springs, so the timber pier is usable from about half five to nine. That's the window, regardless of fog. If the fog holds past nine, the next useful tide is the evening one, and nobody will land in the dark. That's the arithmetic, and it doesn't care what any of us hope.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Added. Met Office: fog forming after midnight, 'confidence in the timing of clearance is low'. Sound Lines: final check at 05:00; the relief vessel 'will not carry passengers'. Coastguard: decision early tomorrow, published on its page; 'please do not gather at Gilliver or Port Ammet slipways'. I will post the decision here when it is published, whichever way it goes. Pell.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: The relief vessel is a separate boat with a separate crew. The 07:10 should run as timetabled, subject to the same fog as everyone else. If there's any change it will be on the Sound Lines page, not on here. Please don't come to the slipway to watch. Answered, and back to my charts.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: So it's all on the fog. Convenient. If they don't go I'll be asking why, and I'll keep asking. And if they do go, I'll be asking why it took five days. Either way somebody owes those people an explanation, and it isn't the ferry company.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: On that last sentence, Gil, we agree completely, and I'll sign whatever letter you write to Grieve, provided you leave the anonymous sources out of it and put your own name at the bottom.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: I asked on here a little while ago whether the young people on the island had a lamp. I still don't know. But if they look this way tonight there will be no dark window on this side of the water. I have done all I can do, which is the lamps and the kettle. Maud

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Driving up to Gilliver tonight with a van full of tins from the school in Port Ammet and two big work lights off my trailer for the hall car park. Not for the slipway, Rook's already told me where I can put them. I'll be the bloke in the hi-vis making tea. No job too small.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Last one from me for the list: the 07:10 is running tomorrow 'subject to fog'. I've booked the day off anyway. I'll be at the end of Lisle pier at first light, which isn't Gilliver and isn't the Holm, but you can see the east approaches from there on a clear morning. Not that it'll be clear.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 20:00 reading: air 2.6 C, dew point 1.9 C, calm, sky clear. Visibility from the point still 25 km, the Holm lights plain across the water. A fog bank was visible on the southern horizon at sunset, low and flat. Whether it comes in or sits there I genuinely can't tell you. Going to bed early with an alarm for four.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: We've put a lamp in the front window. My partner said 'we're not Gilliver' and I said no, but they don't know that from the island. The kids argued about whose turn it is to check the wick. I've told them it stays lit till the radio says something, whatever it says.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Fog bank sitting off to the south. Holm lights on, three, steady. I'll keep my lamp lit. Not going out in the morning, the Coastguard asked us all to stay in. First time in forty year I've been asked. I'll be on the quay wall with the rest, whatever the lass from the hall says.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Alright. I've been a prat on this thread. My lad's mate's dad is one of the volunteers on the boat, it turns out, and he's been round ours twice this week. So I'm hoping, like everyone. If it all goes fine I'll still say I told you so, but quietly.

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: Sorry to post again. I'm on my way in to work. The fog's come in now, thick at the slipway end, thinner up by the hall. I can still see a light on the Holm if I stand by the chapel, just the one from here. I might be wrong. I'm going to stop posting on this thread and just look.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Trials yesterday, for the record: she held 11 knots, steering's heavy, bearings ran cool, both ladders deploy in under a minute, floodlights work. Spare VHF, two first-aid kits, blankets from the hall, flasks from Rook. Fuelled and alongside at Port Ammet. Now it's up to the fog, and I can't fix fog. I'll be in the engine room either way.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Crew rested, vessel ready, plan agreed. Final weather check at 05:00. If we can't see the pier we don't go in, and if we don't go in we'll say so plainly. I'd ask the harbour not to cheer if we sail and not to boo if we don't. Turning in early.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Height, dark coat, no light: that's what I saw at the slipway, and I'll still say it to anyone. What I'll see tomorrow I don't know. Bow, lines, ladders. If the pier's there and people are on it, I'll get them aboard. That's the whole of what I can promise, and I'm not promising the fog.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: We're not fishing tomorrow, skipper says the Coastguard wants the water clear. I'll be at home with the lamp on. I told my mum about the other thing tonight, the whole of it, first time. She didn't laugh. That's all I'm saying on here.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: Chandlery open from five. Coffee's free, mops are for watchers. Lads, whatever happens in the morning, the boat crew are ours and they get a quiet harbour to come back to. No phones in their faces. I mean it, and I'll be stood at the top of the slip to make sure.

units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: Calm tonight, the sea like poured lead. No walkers on the cliff path, or none where the beam stops. I read that people in your Sound are leaving lamps in every window for the crew on the island. I lit the small brass lamp in the watch room and set it on the sill facing north, which is the wrong direction by half a world, but I think direction matters less than intent.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: update: supervisor sent chapter four back with only nine comments, which in thesis terms is a love letter. also I put a desk lamp in the lab window for the island people, because everyone on here is. the corridor lights came on for nobody again at one, but honestly tonight it felt like company.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Log, 00:40: patrolled east gate, nil found. The fox sat by the light pole again and I left it a biscuit, which is against policy. Somebody on the day shift has taped a paper lamp to the monitor bank with 'for the island' written on it. Supervisor says leave it. 02:00 tea.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Bakery update: I've put a little oil lamp on the shop counter tonight, facing the street, because people on here are doing it for those folk in the north and I liked the thought. The van at the edge of the streetlight hasn't been back since the sleeping man. A batch of seeded loaves came out perfect. Bread is a kind of hope with a crust.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Overnight show tonight was the quietest I've ever produced. People rang to say where they were and what lamp they'd lit: a trucker in a lay-by, a nurse in Lisle, a man in Brackwater with a bicycle light on his windowsill. I'm still not buying any of the stories. I've already left the studio lights on. Tonight I turned on the car park ones too.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Shift's done. Harri asked if the island folk had got off yet. Not yet, I said, tomorrow maybe, there's fog. He said fog's good for nothing but hiding in. Then he said sorry, he didn't mean anything by it, it's just what his father used to say. We left the bus lights on when we got off. Driver didn't mind.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: I rang tonight, Orla, and got through, and said only that the bookshop window has a lamp in it now. You put me on for nine seconds. Thank you. The fog is down over Tollinby too, so thick the streetlights are just little moons. Gently, everyone, and good luck in the morning to the people on the boat.

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear neighbours, I have put my late husband's brass lamp in the window of 7C, facing north, though I cannot see the sea from here. I took the stairs down this morning to look at the tealights on the landing, for the first time since the summer. They were all still lit. I did not hear anything but my own feet. Irena, 7C

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Hello all. Some of you have put tealights on the 6-8 landing for the island crew. That's lovely. The caretaker says he'll allow it for this week if they're in jars and nobody props the fire door. Hassan is selling jars at cost. The friend on 4 asked me to say thank you, and that's all she asked me to say. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Jars sold out by nine, so I've given away the pickle jars from the back, washed. If the lady on 4, or her friend, needs a lift to Gilliver early tomorrow, my cousin is driving up at four with the bread van and has a spare seat. She only has to ask. H

units.title: Gilliver front, dusk (catalogued, nothing odd)
units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Posting the link to the catalogue entry for the Gilliver front recording rather than the file, at the cataloguer's suggestion. Daylight and dusk only, I promised myself that. It's people and a kettle and a dog. I recorded it because I wanted something to remember this week by that wasn't a headline. Make of it what you will.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so I listened twice, and at about 18 minutes someone on the wall says 'there's still a light' and someone else says 'aye', and that's my favourite moment in any recording on this forum. glad you went in daylight. glad you came home. see you at the reservoir in spring.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Thank you, dunlin. This is exactly what LowBand is for. Pinning it for the week. Everyone else: if you're in the Sound tonight, stay in, keep warm, and let the boat crews do their work in the morning without an audience.
